title: Corn, canned, cooked with butter or margarine

content.title: About
content.content: Corn, canned, cooked with butter or margarine (code 4680) is a ready‑to‑eat product made from mature sweet corn kernels that are boiled, mixed with butter or margarine, and sealed in airtight cans. The product retains a sweet flavor, tender texture, and a buttery aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canned corn is a staple side dish in American and European cuisines because it requires no preparation.
Adding butter or margarine improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin A and K.
Corn is one of the few vegetables that naturally contains appreciable amounts of carotenoids, giving it a golden hue.
In the United States, over 70 % of all canned vegetables are corn varieties.
Corn was one of the first domesticated crops, cultivated by humans more than 7,000 years ago.

items.title: Good source of dietary fiber
items.content: Corn provides fiber that supports healthy digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The product contains thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Carotenoids
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin help maintain eye health and protect against age‑related macular degeneration.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Corn supplies magnesium, potassium, and iron, essential for muscle function and blood formation.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Its carbohydrate content provides a quick source of energy, while the added fats make the dish more satiating.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Canned foods often contain added salt; people monitoring sodium intake should choose low‑salt versions.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Although uncommon, corn allergy can cause skin rashes, swelling, and respiratory symptoms.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sweet corn naturally contains sugars; individuals with diabetes should watch portion sizes.

items.title: Trans fats in margarine
items.content: If prepared with margarine, the product may contain trans fats, which should be limited.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Corn can be eaten straight from the can, added to salads, soups, pasta, omelets, or used as a filling for tacos and burritos. Warm it briefly in a skillet with a little butter for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened cans in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer the corn to an airtight container and keep it refrigerated for up to 3–4 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
